roomPresets.title: Indian 1-BHK Studio
roomPresets.subtitle: Compact 140 sq.ft bedroom requiring storage and light

analysis.spatialLayout: Narrow floor circulation pinched between wardrobe and bed. Shifting clothes storage into high-level vertical cabinets opens up a 90 cm perimeter walkway.
analysis.naturalLight: Strong direct sunlight from north-facing balcony window. Layer translucent white linen shears to diffuse heat while keeping the study desk luminous.
analysis.storageDeclutter: Clear loose books and chargers using the IKEA SKÅDIS wall pegboard and under-bed rolling drawers, freeing 35% more usable floor area.
analysis.paletteMaterials: Blonde birch veneer and pale ash pair harmoniously with sage green linen accents, creating a calm visual sanctuary in a bustling urban context.
analysis.budgetStrategy: Allocate ₹20,000 to multifunctional birch storage, ₹15,000 to ergonomic seating and desk, and ₹10,000 to soft textiles and layered lighting.
analysis.designSummary: A light-filled Scandinavian sanctuary transforming a compact Mumbai/Bengaluru studio into an uncluttered haven of peace and productivity.
analysis.notice: Verified architectural case study for compact urban apartments.

roomPresets.title: Urban Family Living
roomPresets.subtitle: 190 sq.ft lounge with dispersed furniture and cord tangle

analysis.spatialLayout: Centrally crowded arrangement causes visual fatigue. Aligning seating along a single clean sightline toward the balcony enhances perceived depth by 40%.
analysis.naturalLight: Ceiling lighting is too harsh and directional. Replace with a 3-layer Nordic ambient plan: 1 soft floor uplight, 1 low reading task lamp, and warm sconces.
analysis.storageDeclutter: Open TV console gathers clutter. Transition to flush BESTÅ cabinets with discreet cable grommets to cleanly mask multimedia boxes.
analysis.paletteMaterials: Warm chalk walls, solid ash accents, and tactile flatwoven jute rugs ground the space with organic wabi-sabi composure.
analysis.budgetStrategy: Direct ₹28,000 toward closed low-line media storage, ₹22,000 toward focal lounge seating, and ₹15,000 toward natural jute rug and warm lighting.
analysis.designSummary: An airy Japandi living room that eliminates visual noise while maintaining warm hospitality for family gatherings.
analysis.notice: Verified architectural case study for residential living rooms.

roomPresets.title: Balcony / Study Nook
roomPresets.subtitle: 75 sq.ft study corner with screen glare and loose paperwork

analysis.spatialLayout: Desk directly opposes window causing eye fatigue. Angle work surface 90 degrees perpendicular to window wall to invite side illumination.
analysis.naturalLight: Strong ambient contrast between computer display and dark corners. Add a dimmable HEKTAR task lamp positioned above eye level.
analysis.storageDeclutter: Introduce vertical modular KALLAX cubes to keep binders and electronics off desk surface, leaving workspace pristine.
analysis.paletteMaterials: Matte powder-coated charcoal steel, exposed grain pine, and deep fjord blue linen harmonize for deep focus.
analysis.budgetStrategy: Allocate ₹14,000 to ergonomic desk & task chair, ₹12,000 to vertical wall storage, and ₹9,000 to glare-free lighting.
analysis.designSummary: A distraction-free Nordic work alcove maximizing small spaces with industrial Scandinavian precision.
analysis.notice: Verified architectural case study for residential work nooks.
